qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Global oilseed processing and grain origination network provides physical scale and logistics presence, but offers no structural pricing power. Operates as a pure commodity price-taker whose operating margins (2-3%) and ROIC (10Y avg ~7%, FY24 7.1%, FY25 3.6%) are governed by volatile, cyclical soybean and softseed crush spreads rather than proprietary economic rents. Return on capital consistently falls below the 12% hurdle across the cycle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Global agricultural processor and merchandiser operating as a commodity price-taker. Despite vast origination and crushing scale enhanced by the Viterra acquisition, Bunge lacks pricing power over fungible agricultural commodities. Operating margins average 2-3% and multi-cycle ROIC (~7% 10-year average, falling to ~3.6% in 2025) fails the 12% hurdle. Margins remain hostage to industry crush spreads and volatile working-capital swings.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle financial track record shows 10-year average ROIC of ~6.95% (5-year median ~10.2%, dropping to ~7.09% in FY2024 and ~3.62% in FY2025), failing the 12% hurdle. Gross margins are paper-thin at 4.5%-6.5% and operating margins average 2%-3%, occasionally turning negative during agricultural down-cycles (e.g. 2019). July 2025 acquisition of Viterra ($10.6B total consideration including $5.34B stock and $3.55B debt absorption) expands scale in grain handling and origination but increases capital intensity and leverage while leaving the core price-taking commodity economics unchanged. Bunge cannot unilaterally raise prices above global market-clearing levels without immediate customer defection.
